assessment: Scientific review retained the source-supported vortex-number fit. The equilibration-time candidate was rejected because the raw abstraction misread a fit uncertainty as an additional linear term. The two energy-spectrum candidates were rejected because they did not satisfy the executable contract. Public wording was de-identified, and the counterfactual exponent was authored outside the reported fit uncertainty; neither change is attributed to the paper.

candidates.title: Vortex formation after a finite-time quench
candidates.claim: At equilibration, the simulated vortex count is fitted by n_v = 249.036 * tau_q^(-0.534) for quench durations from 10 to 1000.

source.citation: Seong-Ho Shinn et al., Spontaneous Quantum Turbulence in a Newborn Bose-Einstein Condensate via the Kibble-Zurek Mechanism, Physical Review Letters (2026), DOI:10.1103/b16v-hwp2
source.locator: Figure 1(c) and main-text fit immediately below the equilibration-time fit
source.role: The central fitted relation and reported quench-duration domain define the paper-grounded world.

apparatus.name: spgpe_simulator
apparatus.description: A two-dimensional stochastic projected Gross-Pitaevskii simulation of condensate formation after a finite-time quench.

candidates.background: A two-dimensional Bose gas is driven through a continuous transition. The quench duration can be selected, and the number of vortices is counted when the condensate reaches equilibration.
initial_observations: A quench duration of 10 produces about 73 vortices at equilibration.
A quench duration of 100 produces about 21 vortices at equilibration.
A quench duration of 1000 produces about 6 vortices at equilibration.

controls.name: tau_q
controls.description: Duration of the linear quench in the simulation's dimensionless time units.

readouts.name: n_v
readouts.description: Vortex count at equilibration, represented by the central fitted response.

notes: The paper-grounded world is the deterministic central fit, not a claim that individual stochastic simulation runs are noise-free.
All simulation settings other than quench duration remain fixed.
The alternative-world exponent is benchmark-authored and is not a claim made by the source paper.
candidates.counterfactual_change: Only exponent changes, from the paper-fit value -0.534 to the benchmark-authored value -0.25; amplitude remains 249.036.
